skill.name: extension-stripe
skill.description: Adds Stripe checkout guidance for Caffeine AI apps, including Motoko backend setup, admin configuration, and frontend payment routing.
skill.summary: Add Stripe checkout sessions, payment status pages, and admin payment setup to Caffeine AI apps.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: The static shell, filesystem, network, and reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation links, and code examples. Manual review found payment workflow risks: caller-controlled checkout inputs, caller-controlled redirect URLs, application-state storage of a Stripe secret key, and unauthenticated payment status lookup.

remediation.suggestion: Create checkout sessions from server-side product IDs and stored prices. Validate quantity, currency, and success or cancel URL origins before calling Stripe.
Use a platform secret store or encrypted configuration path. Restrict admin updates, avoid logging the value, and document key rotation.
Require caller ownership or admin permission before returning payment status. Avoid exposing userPrincipal or raw provider responses unless needed.

static_findings.snippet: There is the prefabricated module `mo:caffeineai-stripe/stripe.mo` that that cannot be modified. It
* If not, opens an admin panel and asks the user to initialze Stripe with `StripeConfiguration`.
* Note that JSON parsing of backend `createCheckoutSession` result is needed.
* Validate that the parsed session includes a non-empty `url`. If missing, throw an error and do not
* Redirect webpage to url in `CheckoutSession`: This allows the user to complete the payment.
* Do NOT use router navigation for the Stripe URL. Use `window.location.href`.
* Never navigate to `/undefined`; if `session.url` is missing, show an error and stop.

semantic_findings.title: Client-Controlled Checkout Session Inputs
semantic_findings.description: The sample backend accepts shopping items, successUrl, and cancelUrl from the caller and forwards them to Stripe. Without server-side product and origin validation, clients can alter prices, quantities, currency, or redirect targets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The public checkout function directly forwards caller-supplied items and URLs to Stripe. The file does not show a server-side product lookup, price validation, or redirect allowlist before session creation.

semantic_findings.title: Stripe Secret Stored In Application State
semantic_findings.description: The Stripe configuration includes a secretKey and the sample stores the full configuration in an actor variable. The guide does not describe encryption, an external secret store, rotation, or disclosure controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The secret field and state assignment are explicit in the example. Deployment-specific protections may exist, so the confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Payment Status Access Lacks Caller Authorization
semantic_findings.description: The sample exposes getStripeSessionStatus(sessionId) without checking caller ownership or admin permission. This can allow payment status probing or disclosure if session IDs are learned.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The status function is public and takes only a session ID. Session ID entropy reduces exploitability, but no ownership or admin check is shown.

content.user_title: Add Stripe Payments to Caffeine Apps
content.value_statement: Caffeine app teams need a repeatable way to add card payments without writing every Stripe flow from scratch. This skill provides backend and frontend guidance for checkout sessions, payment status pages, and admin Stripe setup.
actual_capabilities: Describes Motoko types for Stripe configuration, shopping items, checkout sessions, and session status.
Shows admin-gated backend functions for product changes and Stripe configuration.
Provides a frontend checkout hook that creates Stripe sessions and validates the returned URL.
Guides browser redirects to Stripe Checkout with payment success and failure handling.
Specifies TanStack Router paths for payment success and payment failure pages.
limitations: It does not provide complete production-ready frontend components.
It does not validate product pricing or redirect URLs on the backend by default.
It requires the Caffeine AI authorization extension and Motoko package dependencies.
It leaves Stripe secret storage controls to the application author.

use_cases.title: Launch paid Caffeine features
use_cases.description: Add credit and debit card checkout to a Caffeine AI application with backend Stripe session support.

use_cases.title: Connect checkout screens
use_cases.description: Link frontend checkout actions to backend session creation and payment result routes.

use_cases.title: Plan payment readiness

prompt_templates.title: Add basic checkout
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new paid app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Stripe payment skill to add credit and debit card checkout to my Caffeine AI app. Include backend setup and payment result pages.

prompt_templates.title: Configure admin setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Add controlled Stripe configuration for administrators.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an admin Stripe setup flow that asks for the secret key and allowed countries only when Stripe is not configured.

prompt_templates.title: Connect frontend checkout
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a checkout flow that creates a Stripe session, validates the returned URL, and routes success and failure pages with TanStack Router.

prompt_templates.title: Harden payment security
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the Stripe integration for price tampering, unsafe redirect URLs, secret handling, and payment status access control. Recommend concrete fixes.

output_examples.input: A developer asks Claude to add card checkout to a Caffeine AI shop.
output: Backend payment setup is added with admin-only Stripe configuration.
Checkout flow creates a session and redirects only after a valid URL is returned.
Success and failure routes are defined for the payment result.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks Codex to harden the generated payment flow.
output: Price calculation moves to trusted backend product records.
Success and cancel URLs are restricted to approved origins.
Payment status checks require caller ownership or administrator access.

best_practices: Validate product IDs, prices, quantities, and currencies on the backend before creating a Stripe session.
Store Stripe secret keys through a protected secret-management path and limit administrator access.
Show clear payment success, failure, and retry states after Stripe redirects back to the app.
anti_patterns: Do not trust client-provided prices or product descriptions when creating checkout sessions.
Do not redirect to a checkout URL unless the backend response includes a valid Stripe URL.
Do not expose payment status to callers who do not own the Stripe session.

faq.question: What does this skill add?
faq.answer: It guides Stripe checkout integration for Caffeine AI apps, including backend session creation and frontend payment routing.

faq.question: Does it include complete UI components?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples that developers adapt to their app.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use this skill as implementation guidance.

faq.question: Does it require other Caffeine AI extensions?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on the Caffeine AI authorization extension and related Motoko packages.

faq.question: Can it handle Stripe Checkout redirects?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to redirect users to Stripe and route success or failure pages.

faq.question: What should I secure before production?
faq.answer: Validate backend prices and redirect URLs, protect the Stripe secret key, and restrict payment status checks.
